title: Playing Lake Pontchartrain, Washington Garden and Bucktown
summary: Laine played Sundays and Wednesdays at Washington Garden, an old hotel at the lake, and describes Bucktown's dancing pavilions and the crowds.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Yeah. Yeah. I see. Very nice. Mm-hmm. Did you play out at Ponchertrain at all? For the camps? Do where? Out at Ponchertrain, out on the lake? Oh, man. I played Sundays and Wednesdays at the lake.

I played at the Washington Garden at the lake. I played Sunday and Wednesdays at the lake. I played at the Washington Garden at the lake. Washington Garden at the lake on a Wednesday, and Sundays I played private picnics. What was Washington Garden? Was that a campground or something? No, it was an old hotel. On the shore? On the shore. An old hotel. Yeah. It was wonderful in my young days. That place was, the Washington Hotel at Millenburg. It was a wonderful, wonderful place. What were the toughest parts where you used to play? Was Bucktown pretty tough in those days? Bucktown? They had dancing pavilions. They did? Yeah. They had two pretty good dancing pavilions at Bucktown.
What kind of people came to, what were the people like that lived out there? What kind of people were they?

Pretty nice people, all nice people, but most of the people was from the city. I see. They'd come out to hear the band? Yes, they'd come out there, you know. Come out there in street cars and hikes and stuff like that, you see.
